summary: Documents the Agent Circuit Breaker reliability pattern: wrapping agent subprocess calls in retry-with-backoff and a circuit that opens after N consecutive failures, preventing cascading failures and eliminating manual intervention for transient errors. MAST study found 41–86.7% real-task failure rates in multi-agent systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses ProcessRunner AgentTimeoutError → AIBlocked gap with no retry; implementing this pattern at the AgentRunner layer requires minimal architectural change

source: LLM Agent Cost Attribution: Complete Production 2026 Guide — digitalapplied.com
summary: Production guide documenting five token cost attribution layers for LLM agents: per-request token counts, per-session rolling budgets, per-stage latency, model-tier routing signals, and cost circuit-breakers. References November 2025 incident where four agents ran for 11 days generating a $47,000 API bill.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge stores zero cost or latency data; ai_runs has no token/cost columns; ProcessResult.durationMs exists in memory but is never persisted to the DB

source: CodeTracer: Towards Traceable Agent States — arXiv 2604.11641
summary: Framework for converting heterogeneous agent run directories into structured hierarchical traces, automatically identifying the earliest failure-critical stage in a trajectory. Produces actionable debugging signals that can be fed back via reflective replay, enabling targeted recovery from earlier mistakes.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge has zero cross-run memory; after RESET_TO_TODO agents repeat the same failed approaches; spool-dir log files and RunEventEmitter 8KB buffer are the raw data sources for trace extraction

source: Runtime Execution Traces Guided Automated Program Repair — arXiv 2604.02647
summary: Shows that agents given their own past execution traces as context resolve 32% more defects than agents starting from scratch. Validates injecting failure trace context into remediation prompts as a concrete, measurable improvement to repair quality.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — companion inspiration for HID-164; validates the 32% improvement claim for trace-guided remediation; AddressingReview stage is the direct beneficiary

summary: Fastest-growing open-source agent framework in 2026 (~105k stars). Implements a closed learning loop: after 5+ tool calls, a background process condenses the trajectory into a SKILL.md artifact (YAML frontmatter + Markdown procedure). An autonomous Curator cron scores, merges, and prunes the skill library weekly. June 2026 added /learn command for real-time skill capture.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — the SKILL.md pattern maps to AgentForge's artifact model; after each completed run, the orchestrator could emit skill artifacts to a persistent skills directory and inject them into subsequent Planning prompts. The Curator pattern translates to a Fastify background job.

source: PASTE — Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution — arXiv 2603.18897
summary: Learns recurring control-flow patterns in agent tool-call sequences and speculatively fires the next tool call before the LLM has decided to issue it. Semantically lossless: logical execution order is preserved. Results: 48.5% reduction in average task completion time, 1.8x tool execution throughput, 61.9% reduction in p99 tail latency.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — applies to intra-subprocess tool dispatch (Claude Code's internal tool calls) rather than AgentForge's cross-stage orchestration; would require forking or patching Claude Code CLI internals, which is out of scope. Worth revisiting if Claude Code adds MCP hook points.

source: BAVT — Budget-Aware Value Tree Search — arXiv 2603.12634
summary: Models multi-hop agent reasoning as a dynamic search tree with budget-conditioned node selection: the remaining resource ratio (tokens used / tokens budgeted) is used as a scaling exponent, creating a parameter-free transition from exploration to exploitation. BAVT under strict low-budget constraints outperforms baseline agents with 4x the resource budget.
relevanceToAgentForge: High conceptually — injecting remaining-budget ratio into state transition decisions is directly actionable. However, the per-run cost telemetry (HID-163) must be built first to compute the ratio. Marked considered_not_selected; revisit once HID-163 ships.

summary: Proposes a stream paradigm where agent execution and user intervention are concurrent on a bidirectional channel. Introduces a reversibility taxonomy (Idempotent/Reversible/Compensable/Irreversible) for agent actions and the Revision Absorber algorithm (Earliest-Conflict Rollback) that minimizes wasted work on revision. Matches brute-force restart quality at a fraction of the cost.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — the reversibility taxonomy directly applies to AgentForge state transitions (e.g., file writes = Compensable; API calls = Irreversible). Would require adding checkpoint snapshots before non-Idempotent transitions. Scope is significant; flagged for a future sprint after core reliability (HID-162) lands.

source: Letta (formerly MemGPT) — Three-Tier Agent Memory — github.com/letta-ai/letta
summary: Rearchitected agent memory system with three tiers: core memory (always in-context), recall memory (searchable conversation history via semantic search), and archival memory (long-term cold storage). April 2026 launch of Letta Code desktop app. Production pattern: vector store (fast fuzzy recall) + episodic buffer + knowledge graph.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the simpler cross-run failure injection (HID-164) addresses the most acute memory gap without requiring a vector store. Full three-tier memory is a larger initiative; the recall memory tier could power cross-issue pattern retrieval in a future sprint.

summary: ByteDance's open-source long-horizon SuperAgent harness; #1 GitHub Trending Feb 28 2026 with 89k+ stars. Built on LangGraph. Lead agent dynamically spawns sub-agents at runtime, each with scoped context, tools, and termination conditions. V2.0 ships a virtual computer (filesystem + bash) and a context engineering layer.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Python-based and relies on LangGraph; architectural patterns (dynamic sub-agent spawning, scoped context) are reference material but not directly portable to AgentForge's TypeScript + CLI subprocess model. The virtual computer concept is worth watching for future sandbox integration.

summary: TypeScript-native (97.5% TS) multi-agent framework with 6,600+ stars. Runtime DAG planning: Coordinator builds a task graph at execution time. Plans are emitted as inspectable, replayable data structures. Supports Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, Bedrock; MCP support; Vercel AI SDK compatible.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — closest TypeScript-native architectural peer to AgentForge. The DAG-as-replayable-data pattern is relevant to AgentForge's future direction. Source code worth studying for runtime planning and Coordinator design patterns.

source: ProRL Agent by NVIDIA — Decoupled Rollout-as-a-Service — arXiv 2603.18815
summary: Standalone HTTP service exposing the RL rollout lifecycle as an API, decoupling rollout orchestration from the training loop via an async three-stage assembly line (INIT/RUN/EVAL worker pools). Qwen3-8B improved from 9.6% to 18.0% on SWE-Bench Verified with RL training. Open-sourced as NVIDIA NeMo Gym.
relevanceToAgentForge: High future potential — each complete state machine traversal is a rollout; structuring AgentForge as a decoupled rollout server from the start would enable attaching a ProRL-compatible RL training pipeline later without architectural changes. Too early until trajectory serialization format is standardized.

source: KAIJU — Executive Kernel for Intent-Gated Execution — arXiv 2604.02375
summary: Separates the LLM (stateless planner invoked only at plan/reflect/aggregate checkpoints) from an execution kernel that handles dependency-aware parallel tool dispatch, scheduling tools with no dependencies simultaneously. Reduces LLM call frequency while maintaining correctness.
relevanceToAgentForge: High conceptually — the LLM-as-stateless-planner model is exactly what AgentForge implements at a coarser granularity. Applying KAIJU's dependency-aware parallel dispatch within a single agent stage (e.g., parallel file reads during Planning) would require surfacing subprocess tool-level APIs. Too early given AgentForge's CLI subprocess model.

source: Mem-π: Adaptive Memory through Learning When and What to Generate — arXiv 2605.21463
summary: RL-trained memory system that jointly decides WHEN to generate guidance and WHAT to generate, using a decision-content decoupled RL objective. Abstains when generation would not help; produces concise guidance otherwise. Achieves 30%+ relative improvement on web navigation tasks vs retrieval baselines.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium future potential — the abstention mechanism (don't inject memory when it's not useful) is architecturally superior to always-inject approaches like HID-164's static last-N-summaries. However, requires training a specialized model, which is out of scope for 1-2 sprint implementation. Revisit after HID-164 is validated.

summary: Protocol standard exposing model-level properties as first-class primitives: rich identity cards with quality hints, progressive payload modes, governed sessions with persistent context, structured provenance tracking, and trust domains. Identity-aware routing achieves ~12x lower latency on easy tasks; semantic frames reduce token count 37% with no quality loss.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — LDP's agent identity card concept is directly applicable to describing Claude Code CLI vs Codex CLI as protocol objects with quality hints and capability tags. However, this requires a multi-agent setup with a routing layer; AgentForge's current static mapping is sufficient until dynamic model routing becomes a priority.

source: FlashAgents — Inter-Agent Streaming and Incremental Prefill — MLSys 2026 Oral
summary: Built on SGLang: streams tokens from agent N to agent N+1 at generation time for incremental prefill during decode phase. Also implements intra-turn radix-tree prefix caching. Results: 40% end-to-end latency reduction, 3.5x speedup in two-agent benchmarks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — FlashAgents optimizes at the inference server layer (GPU KV cache management), not at the orchestration layer. AgentForge uses Claude Code and Codex as externally-hosted API services; the inference stack is not in scope for AgentForge enhancements.

source: SkillOpt-Lite — Self-Evolution via One Line — arXiv 2607.03451
summary: Extends Hermes Agent's self-evolution framework with GEPA (Genetic Evolution of Prompt Architectures) and DSPy integration, enabling agents to evolve their own tool descriptions and system prompts, not just their skill files. Results in improved task performance without human curation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — requires DSPy and genetic prompt optimization infrastructure; significantly more complex than the SKILL.md emission pattern alone. Interesting if Hermes skill integration (considered_not_selected) is pursued, but out of scope for a 1-2 sprint issue on its own.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework — Merged AutoGen + Semantic Kernel — github.com/microsoft/agent-framework
summary: 12.2k stars; merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel in Q1 2026. Python and .NET support. Supports sequential, concurrent, handoff, and group collaboration patterns with checkpointing and time-travel debugging.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Python and .NET only; AgentForge is TypeScript/Node.js 22+. Patterns (time-travel debugging, checkpointing) are architecturally interesting but the implementation is not portable. Reference material only.
